idiom_name: deps object / factory-function closure + composition root in the entry module
implementation_notes: Plain JavaScript has no decorator metadata to drive a container, so the idiomatic realization is explicit passing: constructors and functions take a deps object (or individual collaborators), and factory functions close over what they need and return objects whose methods use the closed-over dependencies. What replaces the injector is the entry module - a small composition root that builds the leaves (db client, logger, clock) and passes them down - and tests construct the same factory with fakes, so no module mocking or global registry is needed. Containers exist (NestJS in JS mode, awilix) but add registration indirection the language does not need for typical graphs.
pitfalls: Module-level singletons (an imported db client or logger) defeat the seam: importing the module makes substitution impossible without module mocking.
The deps object must be threaded deliberately; passing the whole composition root down recreates a service locator.
Dependencies that need connect()/close() must be started and drained by the composition root, not by each consumer.
